document.title: APA-CRM Architecture
document.subtitle: C4 views of the APA-CRM system for **architects and new engineers**: context, containers, components and six runtime flows. Written by hand from the eight repositories at their current commits; no Lantern output.

revisions.author: Hand-written from the code
revisions.summary: First version, from Auth-Service `6cb4eda`, CRM-Frontend `0797125`, crm-shared-lib `442bbbb`, Deployment `3857d28`, Discovery-and-Gateway `62649cb`, File-Service `413caa5`, Main-Service `0b59f25` and Notification-Service `0fc0353`.

revisions.author: Independent second pass over the same commits
revisions.summary: Verified every cited claim against the code. Corrected the check-access filter (organization id in effect only from the header), the consequences of publishing before commit, the frontend build risk, the identity-header risk and the reminder pre-conditions; added three risks (cross-organization permission mix-up, unscoped file deletes and creates, organization details readable by any signed-in user). See verification.md.

member.name: Organization member
member.description: Signs up and in, creates or switches between organizations and, as far as their custom per-organization role allows, manages members, roles, invitations, files and tasks; receives real-time notices and email reminders.

properties.access: Custom per-organization role: a resource × action matrix; no fixed role names in the code

invitee.name: Invited user
invitee.description: A registered user invited into an organization: gets the invitation by email and accepts or declines it in the web app while signed in.

properties.access: Becomes a member with the role chosen by the inviter

apa-crm.name: APA-CRM
apa-crm.description: Lets teams do their CRM work inside organizations: membership with custom roles, a shared file tree, tasks with reminders, and real-time and email notifications.

gmail.name: Gmail SMTP
gmail.description: Delivers all of the system's outbound email: invitations, generated passwords, password-reset codes and task reminders.

frontend.name: CRM-Frontend
frontend.description: Browser UI for organizations, members, roles, files and tasks; keeps the tokens in localStorage, adds the Organization-Id header to every call and listens for notices over STOMP.

properties.stack: Angular ^19.2, PrimeNG ^19, Tailwind 4, @stomp/stompjs ^7.2.1, TypeScript ~5.7; built on node:24.3.0-alpine3.22, served by nginx:alpine3.22
properties.port: 4200 in the container (82 on the host in dev compose)

gateway.name: api-gateway
gateway.description: The only public entry point: verifies the JWT, looks up the caller's permissions in the organization, adds identity headers and routes to the services; also merges task lists with user details.

properties.stack: Spring Cloud 2025.0.0 (WebFlux gateway), reactive Redis, jjwt 0.12.6, crm-shared-lib core + rbac 0.2.0-SNAPSHOT

eureka.name: eureka-service
eureka.description: Service registry for the compose deployments: every service registers and lb:// names resolve through it. Single instance, no peers; disabled in Kubernetes.

auth.name: auth-service
auth.description: Identity provider: sign-up, sign-in, refresh tokens and sessions, password reset, the organization role definitions and the per-organization permission cache.

properties.stack: Spring Cloud 2025.0.0, jjwt 0.12.6, yauaa 8.1.0, MapStruct 1.6.3, Spring Data Redis, crm-shared-lib 0.2.0-SNAPSHOT

main.name: main-service
main.description: Core CRM domain: organizations, membership and role assignment, invitations, organization file links, and tasks with priorities, statuses and reminders; publishes the domain events.

properties.stack: Spring Cloud 2025.1.2, OpenFeign, Spring AMQP, JobRunr 8.6.1, MapStruct 1.6.3, crm-shared-lib 0.3.0-SNAPSHOT

file.name: file-service
file.description: Keeps the directory tree and file bytes: uploads, downloads, renames, moves and deletes files, and creates an organization's root directory on request.

properties.stack: Spring Cloud 2025.0.0, Spring Data JPA, Spring AMQP, crm-shared-lib 0.2.1-SNAPSHOT

notification.name: notification-service
notification.description: Turns events into what people see: pushes real-time notices to users and organizations over STOMP and sends every transactional email from templates.

properties.stack: Spring WebSocket (STOMP, SockJS), Thymeleaf, Spring Mail, OpenFeign, Spring AMQP, crm-shared-lib 0.2.5-SNAPSHOT

auth-db.name: auth_db
auth-db.description: Users with BCrypt passwords, roles and their access controls, refresh tokens (sessions) and password-restore requests. Schema by Hibernate ddl-auto=update.

main-db.name: main_db
main-db.description: Organizations, members and their role links, invitations, file links, tasks, priorities and statuses, plus JobRunr's job tables. Schema by Hibernate ddl-auto=update.

file-db.name: file_db
file-db.description: The file metadata tree and the file content itself as LOBs; there is no object store. Schema by Hibernate ddl-auto=update.

redis.name: Redis permission cache
redis.description: Redis 8.4.0 (7.4.4 in dev compose). Per-organization permissions under organization:{o}:user:{u}:permissions (TTL 10 h), with 10 s failure markers and a distributed lock; written by auth-service, read by api-gateway.

x-main-events.name: main-service.events
x-main-events.description: Main-Service's domain events: org.created, org-user.role-changes, org-invitation.created and org.task.remind.

x-file-events.name: file-service.events
x-file-events.description: The reply org.root-dir.created, sent once an organization's root directory exists.

x-auth-event.name: auth-service.event
x-auth-event.description: Email requests from Auth-Service: user.random-password and user.restore-password.

q-send-message.name: notification-service.send-message
q-send-message.description: Published to through the default exchange. In-app notices (CrmNotification) addressed to one user or to a whole organization.

gw-routes.name: Route table
gw-routes.description: Matches seven routes in order and forwards to lb://auth-service, main-service, file-service and lb:ws://notification-service; /api/organizations/*/preview matches none of them.

gw-auth-filter.name: AuthFilter
gw-auth-filter.description: Rejects a request with 401 unless its Bearer JWT is valid, then adds User-Id and User-Login.

gw-check-access.name: Check-access filter
gw-check-access.description: Verifies the JWT, takes the organization id from the Organization-Id header (403 if none; its path pattern is matched against the absolute URI and never applies) and adds a serialized User-Permissions header; leaves allow or deny to the services.

gw-org-files.name: Organization-files filter
gw-org-files.description: For GET and PATCH on /api/files/{id}, asks main-service whether the file belongs to the organization and passes a 4xx back.

gw-jwt.name: JWT verifier
gw-jwt.description: Checks the HMAC signature with the key shared with auth-service and the expiry, and reads the userId and login claims.

gw-permissions.name: Permission lookup
gw-permissions.description: Reads the member's permissions from Redis and on a miss asks auth-service, on a path auth-service does not serve.

gw-composite.name: Tasks composite API
gw-composite.description: Serves /api/composite/organizations/{org}/tasks: forwards to main-service with identity headers and merges in user details from auth-service.

au-sign-in-api.name: Sign-in API
au-sign-in-api.description: Signs users up and in, rotates refresh tokens and logs out; issues 30-minute HS-signed JWTs and stores each refresh token with parsed device info.

au-restore-api.name: Password restore API
au-restore-api.description: Creates and resends 4-digit reset codes (one request per user per 3 h) and checks a code (5 attempts), returning tokens.

au-users-api.name: Users and sessions API
au-users-api.description: Returns and updates the signed-in user's profile and password, searches users by name and lists or ends sessions; trusts the User-Id header.

au-internal-api.name: Internal API
au-internal-api.description: Serves the other services: role create, edit, filter and delete, user lookups, access-token validation (POST /auth/authorize) and a member's permissions.

au-permission-resolver.name: Permission resolver
au-permission-resolver.description: Builds a member's resource/action permissions from their role ids, fetched from main-service, under a Redis lock with a 10 s failure marker.

au-role-sync.name: Role-change consumer
au-role-sync.description: Recomputes and overwrites a member's cached permissions when main-service reports changed roles.

au-permission-cache.name: Permission cache repository
au-permission-cache.description: Reads and writes the permission entries, failure markers and lock in Redis.

au-email-producers.name: Email request publishers
au-email-producers.description: Asks notification-service to email a generated password or a reset code.

ms-org-api.name: Organization API
ms-org-api.description: Lists, previews, creates and updates organizations; creation sets up the Admin and Member roles in auth-service and the creator's membership in one transaction.

ms-membership-api.name: Membership and roles API
ms-membership-api.description: Invites users, accepts and declines invitations, removes members, and creates, edits and assigns organization roles whose definitions live in auth-service.

properties.classes: OrganizationInvitationController, OrganizationUsersController, OrganizationRolesController, OrganizationUserRoleController and their facades

ms-files-api.name: Organization files API
ms-files-api.description: Links File-Service file ids to an organization and returns its root directory; holds no file bytes.

ms-tasks-api.name: Tasks API
ms-tasks-api.description: Creates, filters, updates and deletes tasks and the organization's priorities and statuses, and schedules or cancels each task's reminder job.

ms-internal-api.name: Internal API
ms-internal-api.description: Answers service-to-service questions: a member's role ids, whether a user is a member, whether a file belongs to an organization.

ms-access-guard.name: Access guard
ms-access-guard.description: Rejects a request with 403 unless User-Id is a member of the organization (a database check) and User-Permissions grants the resource and action.

ms-auth-client.name: Auth client
ms-auth-client.description: Calls auth-service's internal API to create, edit, filter and delete roles and to look up users.

ms-producers.name: Event publishers
ms-producers.description: Publishes domain events to main-service.events and in-app notices to notification-service.send-message; the notice sender swallows send errors.

properties.classes: OrganizationCreatedProducer, OrgUserRoleChangedProducer, InvitationCreatedProducer, TaskReminderProducer, shared-lib MessagingService

ms-consumers.name: Organization event consumers
ms-consumers.description: On org.created, creates the 3 default task priorities and 5 default statuses; on org.root-dir.created, records the organization's root directory.

ms-reminder-job.name: Task reminder job
ms-reminder-job.description: At a task's reminderAt, collects the assignee and creator emails, publishes org.task.remind and marks the task reminded.

fs-api.name: File API
fs-api.description: Uploads (multipart, at most 15 MiB), downloads, updates and deletes files and directories under /api/files.

fs-guard.name: Permission guard
fs-guard.description: Rejects a request with 403 unless the User-Permissions header grants FILES with the needed action.

fs-service.name: File tree service
fs-service.description: Applies the file-tree rules: creates files and directories, renames and moves them, and refuses to delete a non-empty directory without forceDelete.

fs-repos.name: File repositories
fs-repos.description: Persist the metadata tree and the content row that shares each file's id.

fs-root-consumer.name: Root-directory consumer
fs-root-consumer.description: Creates "Root <organization name>" when an organization is created and replies with the new directory id.

ns-email-consumers.name: Email consumers
ns-email-consumers.description: Take password, reset-code, invitation and task-reminder requests off their queues and send one email per recipient.

ns-templates.name: Template builder
ns-templates.description: Renders the four HTML email templates, with links built from FRONTEND_URL and due dates in Europe/Kyiv.

ns-email.name: Email sender
ns-email.description: Sends the HTML email; a failed send throws, so the message is requeued and retried (Spring AMQP default); no dead-letter queue is declared.

ns-message-consumer.name: In-app notice consumer
ns-message-consumer.description: Receives each CrmNotification and rejects a failed one without requeueing.

ns-sender.name: Notification sender
ns-sender.description: Pushes a notice to /user/topic/notifications for one user or /topic/organizations/{id}/notifications for an organization.

ns-stomp.name: STOMP endpoint and broker
ns-stomp.technology: Spring WebSocket · SockJS · in-memory simple broker
ns-stomp.description: Accepts client sockets at /ws-notifications and keeps sessions and subscriptions in memory, so only one instance can serve them.

ns-interceptor.name: STOMP auth interceptor
ns-interceptor.description: Authorizes CONNECT through auth-service, checks organization-topic SUBSCRIBE through main-service and rejects any client SEND.

ns-clients.name: Auth and Main clients
ns-clients.description: Call auth-service to validate a token and main-service to check membership.

pages.title: APA-CRM
pages.summary: APA-CRM is a multi-tenant CRM in which each organization defines its own roles and manages members, files and tasks. The most important fact for anyone changing it: **all authorization is decided from headers that api-gateway adds**, so the services trust whatever reaches them.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
This document is for **architects and new engineers**. It was written by hand from the code of the eight APA-CRM repositories at the commits listed under Sources (dates up to 2026-08-23), on 2026-10-29. Lantern produced none of it.

The repositories hold no architecture decision records, owners or quality goals; where this document needs one of those it says *unknown*. People and external systems below are only those the code shows.

items.label: User roles
items.value: Custom
items.note: Defined per organization; none fixed in code

items.label: Owners, quality goals
items.value: Unknown

relationships.label: Manages organizations, members, files and tasks in
Delivers passwords, codes and reminders to

sections.body: Left out on purpose: Docker Hub and JitPack are used only to build and publish (images `aappaa/*`, the shared library), and Prometheus and Grafana only scrape metrics. None takes part in a user request.

sections.title: Sources
rows: none: a library (core, messaging, rbac) built into the services
none: Docker Compose, Helm and Kustomize descriptors

sections.title: Glossary
rows: The tenant: members, roles, files and tasks all belong to one. A user can be in several and switches between them.
A per-organization role is a set of resource × action pairs (resources such as USERS, ROLES, INVITATIONS, FILES, TASKS; actions CREATE, READ, UPDATE, DELETE; ALL as a wildcard).
Request headers the gateway adds after checking the token; the services trust them instead of checking the token again.
Advanced Message Queuing Protocol, spoken by RabbitMQ.
RabbitMQ terms: a producer publishes to an exchange with a routing key; bindings copy the message to queues, which consumers read.
OpenFeign, the declarative HTTP client the services use to call each other.
A token signature made with one secret key shared by signer and checker.
A Java library that stores delayed background jobs in the database and runs them at their due time.
JSON Web Token: the 30-minute access token issued by auth-service.
Large object: a database column holding binary content, here the file bytes.
Load-balanced service names that Spring Cloud resolves to an instance through the service registry.
The mail-sending protocol, upgraded to TLS on port 587.
Single-page application: the Angular app that runs in the browser.
Simple Text Oriented Messaging Protocol, a pub/sub protocol run over a WebSocket.

sections.title: No recorded decisions
sections.body: None of the eight repositories has architecture decision records or design documents. The decisions below are observed in code and configuration; their rationale is *not recorded* unless a README states it.

items.title: Authorization at the gateway; services trust headers
items.body: api-gateway verifies the JWT and adds `User-Id` and `User-Permissions`; the services check those headers, not the token. Rationale: Main-Service's README says authorization is expected at the gateway (`Main-Service/README.md:70`).

items.title: One PostgreSQL schema per service
items.body: auth_db, main_db and file_db, each written only by its service. Compose runs three PostgreSQL containers; Kustomize puts all three in one instance. Rationale: not recorded.

items.title: Shared HMAC key for access tokens
items.body: auth-service signs HS JWTs and the gateway checks them with the same `auth.token.signing.key`; refresh tokens are opaque strings in auth_db. Rationale: not recorded.

items.title: Permissions cached in Redis, refreshed by events
items.body: auth-service writes each member's permissions to Redis (TTL 10 h); the gateway reads them; `org-user.role-changes` triggers a recompute. Rationale: not recorded.

items.title: One topic exchange per producing service
items.body: main-service.events, file-service.events and auth-service.event; most queues are declared by both producer and consumer. Rationale: not recorded.

items.title: File bytes in PostgreSQL
items.body: file-service keeps content as LOBs in file_db and serves it from memory; no object store exists in any deployment. Rationale: not recorded.

items.title: Delayed reminders with JobRunr
items.body: main-service schedules a one-off job per task reminder, stored in main_db. Rationale: not recorded.

items.title: Shared library for cross-cutting code
items.body: crm-shared-lib (core, messaging, rbac) is pulled from JitPack as a SNAPSHOT at a different version by each service. Rationale: not recorded.

items.title: Compose for local and dev, Helm for Kubernetes
items.body: Rationale recorded: Compose for local and development, Helm for "Kubernetes production" (`Deployment/README.md:18-21`).

sections.title: Risks and findings
rows: Identity headers are trusted and never stripped. The gateway does not remove client-sent `User-Id` or `User-Permissions` on its public routes (`/api/auth/**`, `/api/restore-password-request/**`, `/ws-notifications/**`), and `/api/internal/**` has no authentication; only the route table keeps it private.

Anyone who reaches a service directly on the network can act as any user with any permission. Through the gateway this is latent today: the public routes lead only to endpoints that ignore these headers.

The check-access filter takes the organization from the `Organization-Id` header, never from the path: its pattern `^/api/organizations/(\d+)…` is matched against the absolute request URI. main-service checks membership in the path's organization but the permission in the header, which is computed for the header's organization.

A member of an organization can probably act there with the permissions they hold in another organization, for example one they created themselves (Admin = ALL:ALL), by sending that organization's id in the header.
The gateway's permission fallback calls `/users/{u}/organizations/{o}/persmissions` without the `/api/internal` prefix that auth-service serves.
Organization-scoped calls probably fail whenever the Redis entry is missing or has expired (TTL 10 h), until a role change rewrites it.

Secrets: one HMAC signing key shared by gateway and auth-service; Gmail SMTP credentials; generated passwords sent in plaintext through RabbitMQ and email; Hibernate bind parameters logged at TRACE (password hashes, refresh tokens); Helm secrets as plaintext `stringData`; test keys committed.
Whoever holds the signing key can mint tokens for any user; logs and the broker carry credentials.
Events and Feign side effects happen inside database transactions, before commit, with no outbox. Example: organization creation publishes `org.created` before its transaction commits.

Consumers can run before the organization exists: the default priorities and statuses consumers then fail without requeue, leaving the organization without them, while the root-directory reply is requeued and retried until it succeeds; roles created in auth-service are orphaned if the transaction rolls back.
notification-service declares `GET /api/internal/auth/authorize` with a body; auth-service maps `POST`.
It works only because the default Feign HTTP client turns a GET with a body into a POST; changing the client would break every notification socket.
The web app calls `GET /api/organizations/{id}/preview`, which main-service serves, but no gateway route matches it (`*` matches one path segment).
The organization preview probably returns 404 in every deployment.

crm-shared-lib versions differ: gateway and auth-service 0.2.0, file-service 0.2.1, notification-service 0.2.5, main-service 0.3.0 (Boot 4, Jackson 3), all SNAPSHOTs from JitPack. Message classes differ between them.
Builds are not reproducible, and messages from main-service may not deserialize in the older consumers (unverified).
each `pom.xml` near lines 30-33; Auth `OrgUserRoleChangedEvent` vs Main `OrgUserRoleChangedMessage`
Single instances: one Eureka with no peers, one PostgreSQL for all schemas in Kustomize, single Redis and RabbitMQ, one replica of everything in Helm, and an in-memory STOMP broker.
Any one of them failing stops the system; notification-service cannot run more than one instance; gateway authorization depends on Redis and auth-service.

file-service has no notion of organization, and only GET and PATCH on `/api/files/**` get the gateway's ownership check; DELETE and POST check only a FILES permission. Removing a member does not refresh their cached permissions.

Anyone with FILES:DELETE or FILES:CREATE in some organization (their own, for instance) can delete or add files in another organization's tree if they know a file id; a removed member keeps their cached permissions for up to 10 h.
Any member who can read tasks can delete them.
The frontend image is built with `--configuration development`, so it calls `http://localhost:8080`; the production configuration uses a hardcoded LAN IP. The API URL is fixed at build time.
The image only works where the gateway is on the user's own machine.
CORS allows every origin at the gateway, and the Helm ingress combines `*` with credentials.
Browsers reject the Helm combination; the gateway accepts calls from any site.

READMEs are stale: Main-Service says Java 21 and Boot 3; Notification-Service says Java 17 and lists test endpoints and destinations that do not exist; File-Service lists a non-existent internal endpoint; Deployment lists templates, a local frontend and environment variables that do not exist.
New engineers following the READMEs are misled.
`GET /api/organizations/{id}` has no membership check and its gateway route only authenticates.
Any signed-in user can read any organization's details (name, address, email, description) by id.
Schema changes are applied implicitly at startup and cannot be reviewed or rolled back.

sections.title: Unknowns
items: Owners, quality goals and the rationale of most decisions: not recorded.
Which Kubernetes descriptor (Helm or Kustomize) is used in production, and how the web app is served there: no frontend manifest exists and the ingress sends `/` to the gateway.
Whether `lb://` and Feign names actually resolve in Kubernetes with Eureka off: all five services have Spring Cloud Kubernetes on the classpath, but this was not run.
Where the `aappaa/discovery-service` image is built: no workflow builds it.
Whether main-service's 0.3.0 messages deserialize in the consumers on 0.2.x.
The values of the `.env.*` files and secrets, which are not committed.

pages.title: Requests and data
pages.summary: The synchronous view: how a browser request reaches the services through the gateway, which calls the services make to each other, and which store each one owns.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
The Angular app is only served by nginx; the browser then calls **api-gateway** directly on port 8080. The gateway verifies the JWT itself, adds `User-Id`, `User-Login` and, for organization routes, `User-Permissions`, and routes by `lb://` name. Each service owns one PostgreSQL schema except notification-service, which has none.

**crm-shared-lib** is not a container: its core, messaging and rbac modules are compiled into every service (exception mapping, Feign error decoding, the permission aspect, message classes and queue names). Each service pins a different version of it.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Main-Service drives most traffic: organization creation, role changes, invitations and task reminders. File-Service answers `org.created` with `org.root-dir.created`, a request and reply over two exchanges. Notification-Service only consumes. Exchange and queue names are constants in crm-shared-lib, except Auth-Service's exchange, which is a local constant. No dead-letter queues are declared.

pages.title: notification-service
pages.summary: Two paths out: email through Gmail and real-time notices over STOMP. No database and no REST controller.

sections.title: Overview
items: The gateway relays the socket without checking the token; the interceptor checks it with auth-service.
The broker is in memory, so subscriptions live in one instance only.
The README's test REST endpoints and `/user/{userId}/queue/notifications` destination are not in the code.

pages.title: Sign-in and an organization request
pages.summary: A member signs in and then lists the members of their organization. auth-service issues the tokens; on every later call the gateway checks the JWT itself and attaches the member's permissions from Redis. main-service then enforces membership and the permission and asks auth-service for the user details.

items.label: Trigger
items.value: Member submits the login form

items.label: Pre-conditions
items.value: The member has an account and belongs to the organization

items.label: Post-conditions
items.value: Tokens are in localStorage; the member list is shown

steps.message: Checks the BCrypt password, stores a refresh token, signs a 30-minute JWT

steps.info: The app stores them in localStorage and later sends the chosen organization as `Organization-Id`.

steps.message: Lists organization members with the Bearer JWT
Verifies the JWT signature and expiry

steps.info: The path lacks `/api/internal`, which auth-service needs, so this probably returns 404.

pages.title: Create an organization
pages.summary: Creating an organization sets up its Admin and Member roles in auth-service and the creator's membership in one transaction, then announces `org.created`. file-service answers with a root directory over a second exchange, and main-service fills in default task priorities and statuses from its own event. Both events are published before the transaction commits.

items.label: Trigger
items.value: Signed-in user submits the new organization form

items.label: Pre-conditions
items.value: Valid JWT

items.label: Post-conditions
items.value: Organization with Admin and Member roles, the creator as Admin, a root directory, 3 priorities and 5 statuses

steps.message: AuthFilter verifies the JWT and adds User-Id
Opens a transaction and inserts the organization
Adds the creator as a member with the Admin role

steps.note: Published inside the transaction, before commit; no outbox
Before commit, the defaults consumers fail (no requeue); the reply retries

pages.title: Invite a member
pages.summary: A member with INVITATIONS:CREATE invites a registered user. main-service records a pending invitation for 72 hours and hands two messages to RabbitMQ: an invitation email and an in-app notice. notification-service turns them into a Gmail email with a link to the web app and a STOMP push; the invitee later accepts in the web app, which adds them to the organization.

items.label: Trigger
items.value: Inviter submits the invite form

items.label: Pre-conditions
items.value: Inviter is a member whose role grants INVITATIONS:CREATE; the invitee has an account

items.label: Post-conditions
items.value: Pending invitation; invitee has an email and, if connected, an in-app notice

steps.message: Invites a user with a role
Check-access filter: JWT plus permissions from Redis
Stores a PENDING invitation expiring in 72 h
Sends an in-app notice to the invitee

steps.note: Notice send errors are logged and swallowed

Pushes to the invitee if connected

pages.title: Task reminder
pages.summary: Saving a task with a reminder time schedules a JobRunr job that is stored in main_db. At that time main-service's job server looks up the assignee and creator emails in auth-service, publishes `org.task.remind` and marks the task reminded; notification-service sends one Gmail email per recipient.

items.label: Pre-conditions

items.label: Post-conditions
items.value: The creator and the assignee, if any, receive a reminder email; the task is marked reminded

pages.title: Real-time notification
pages.summary: The web app opens one STOMP socket through the gateway, which relays it without checking the token. notification-service authorizes the CONNECT with auth-service and each organization subscription with main-service. Notices from main-service then arrive over RabbitMQ and are pushed to one user or to everyone subscribed to the organization.

items.label: Trigger
items.value: Member opens the web app after sign-in

items.label: Pre-conditions
items.value: Valid JWT; member of the organization

items.label: Post-conditions
items.value: Socket subscribed to the user and organization destinations; notices appear live

Relays the socket, no token check

pages.title: Password reset by email
pages.summary: A user who forgot their password asks for a reset code on a public route. auth-service stores a 4-digit code, at most one request per user every 3 hours, and asks notification-service over RabbitMQ to email it. Entering the right code within 5 attempts returns fresh tokens.

items.label: Trigger
items.value: User submits the forgot-password form

items.label: Pre-conditions
items.value: User has an account and no reset request in the last 3 hours

items.label: Post-conditions
items.value: User is signed in with new tokens

steps.message: Stores a restore request with a 4-digit code

steps.note: Hand-off: the response does not wait for the email

steps.message: Checks the code (at most 5 attempts) and deletes the request
